Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 65 s. 2023 HON. RHETT RONAN T. ANGARA Mayor Municipality of Baler, Aurora Dear Mayor Angara: This pertains to your letter dated April 26, 2023 requesting this Department's opinion on whether or not using SmartPay in the collection of Eco-Tourism Development Fee (SEDF) constitute a violation of Section 130(3) of the Local Government Code. The relevant facts you submitted are as follows: Municipal Ordinance No. 035-2018 was passed by the Sangguniang Bäyan of Baler in order to manage, protect, and conserve the environment and to promote tourism in Baler. Ordinance No. 012-2022 amending some of its provisions and the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) were passed to integrate technological advancement and the safety protocols. Section I (5) of Ordinance No. 012-2022 provides that "Before or upon arrival of guest/s in Baler, electronic payment through Online Platforms shall be authorized upon online application including but not limited to SmartPay." Section 5, Rule 3 of the IRR provides that "Mode of payment and collection. Every tourist, visitor, or patron of the accommodation and other tourism- related establishments in the Municipality of Baler shall pay the SEDF before or upon arrival in Baler at the Municipal Tourism Office, in cash, or through electronic payment, or through online travel application, as may be implemented by the LGU Baler, or any other mode of payment as may be approved by the Municipal Treasurer... Hence, the question on whether there will be a violation of Section 130 (3) of the Local Government Code or any law, if the collection of the SEDF using the Online Tourism Portal and system of collection of SmartPay. Section 130 (3) of R.A. No. 7160, otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991" provides as follows: "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

"The collection of local taxes, fees, charges and other impositions shall in no case be let to any private person;" The system design for SmartPay payment transactions was presented in the letter through a flowchart. However, we cannot sufficiently determine whether the SEDF payments will be directly credited to the LGU's account or not. Thus, in reference to Section 130(3) above, we shall qualify our opinion. If the use of the SmartPay portal constitute a mere payment platform/channel where the LGU concerned will be maintaining an account facilitating an automatic on-time crediting of payments direct to the LGU account, the amount of money paid is deemed collected directly by the government, and not by a private person. There appears to be no violation of Section 130 (3) in this case. On the other hand, if the amount collected will pass though the account of SmartPay provider/supplier before it is remitted to the concerned LGU, the same is deemed to have been collected by a private person (the individual or the juridical person which is the company who owns SmartPay). In such case, the same appears to be in violation of Section 130(3) of the LGC. Hence, your LGU is in the best position to determine which of the foregoing circumstances apply. This opinion is being rendered based on the facts as represented and without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have enlightened you on the matter. Thank you. Very truly yours, th Authority of the Secretary: JUAN ICTOR R. LLAMAS dersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSELLA/JVRL/LLLS-LRALLD/kbm copy furnished. ATTY. ANTHONY C. NUYDA, CESO Ill Regional Director, DILG Region-III Diosdado Macapagal Government Center Maimpis, San Fernando City. Pampanga
